headline: Core Inflation Accelerates

headline_evidence.rule: Official PCE data showed faster annual core inflation.
headline_evidence.data: Core PCE inflation rose 3.3% over the year in October, up from 3.1%.

commentary: Core PCE inflation rose 3.3% from a year earlier in October. The Fed targets 2% inflation over time.

defines.definition: Price changes excluding food and energy across consumer spending.
defines.used_by_and_why: The Fed watches it for underlying inflation trends.

explains.why: It covers a broad range of household spending.

failures: The official release is clearer in concise text.

views.body: Core inflation tracks underlying price changes. Faster gains can strain household budgets.
Price growth remained broad across consumer spending. Cost-conscious buyers may limit optional purchases.
views.keep_wondering: Will demand weaken as prices rise?

views.body: Core PCE inflation remained above the Fed's goal. Rate decisions remain focused on price stability.
views.keep_wondering: Will the Fed raise rates again?

data_note: October core PCE inflation: 0.3% monthly and 3.3% yearly.

headline: Growth Estimate Jumps

headline_evidence.rule: BEA revised third-quarter real GDP substantially higher.
headline_evidence.data: Annualized real GDP growth was revised from 3.4% to 4.3%.

commentary: Real GDP grew at a 4.3% annual rate in the third quarter. The previous estimate was 3.4%.

defines.definition: The total value of goods and services produced domestically.
defines.used_by_and_why: It is the broadest standard measure of economic output.

explains.why: It expresses one quarter's pace as if it continued for a year.
explains.other_reading: The figure describes July through September, not November.

failures: The two official estimates are clearer in text.

views.body: GDP measures total domestic output. Stronger activity can support jobs and incomes.
views.keep_wondering: Will newer data confirm the strength?

views.body: Private domestic demand was revised higher. Corporate profits also increased during the quarter.
The revision shows faster past growth. It does not measure November conditions.
views.keep_wondering: Will current growth remain this strong?

data_note: Third-quarter real GDP: 4.3% annualized, revised from 3.4%.

headline: Consumers Stay Price Sensitive

headline_evidence.rule: Federal Reserve contacts reported cautious discretionary spending.
headline_evidence.data: Consumer spending changed little while households became more selective.

commentary: The Beige Book found little change in consumer spending. Households became choosier about optional purchases.

defines.definition: A Federal Reserve summary of regional business and household conditions.
defines.used_by_and_why: It adds timely, qualitative evidence before policy meetings.

explains.why: These are purchases households can postpone more easily.
explains.other_reading: Tourism was solid while auto sales softened.

failures: Regional evidence is clearer in concise text.

views.body: Households kept spending but watched prices closely. Housing activity weakened as affordability limited demand.
Manufacturing grew modestly while consumer demand stayed uneven. Input costs continued to rise.
views.keep_wondering: Will businesses pass costs to customers?

views.body: Eight districts reported slight to moderate growth. Four reported no change.

data_note: Federal Reserve regional summary collected through November 16.
